lines.say: How much protein do you actually need to build muscle?
A big review pooled forty nine studies of people lifting weights.
Extra protein helped, up to about one point six grams per kilo of body weight a day.
Past that, the benefit mostly flattened out.
So an eighty kilo person needs about one hundred thirty grams a day.
Split it over three or four meals, around thirty to forty grams each.
Chicken, eggs, fish, milk, beans and tofu all count.
Kidney disease? Talk to a doctor before eating high protein.
